entries.title: A write rejected with its resource version unchanged still waits in NEEDS_RECONCILIATION
entries.impact: Fixed in code for the cases where the write can no longer commit; verified live, one run each, for the moved-resourceVersion and replaced-target cases (a plain delete was not run live). Reconciliation is a pure decision table: a deleted or recreated target, or a resourceVersion that moved without this action's evidence, ends SUPERSEDED, which the Coordinator records as FAILED so a new proposal can follow. The live wedge harness (C-EXECUTOR-WEDGE: one run per scenario on one Windows host with kind, 2026-11-11) showed main's Executor (d5b2ed9) staying NEEDS_RECONCILIATION over 5 reconcile passes with the workload still excluded, while 4afc879 resolved the moved-resourceVersion case (rv-race) as SUPERSEDED/ADVANCED_WITHOUT_EVIDENCE and the replaced-target case (delete-recreate) as SUPERSEDED/TARGET_REPLACED, released the workload and applied a second proposal. Still open, and not covered by the harness: kubectl error text is not classified (the DEFINITE_REJECTION and FENCED rows are reserved), so a rejection that leaves the same UID at the same resourceVersion, such as an admission denial, cannot be told apart from a request still in flight. That action stays NEEDS_RECONCILIATION, in doubt until P2.06, and the workload stays excluded from repair; after 600 s the Executor adds one 'Operator action required' result.
entries.workaround: For the unchanged-version case, an operator inspects the Deployment and clears the Executor ledger row by hand. The deleted, recreated and moved-version cases need no workaround.

cites.text: Live write returned an error; reconcile its outcome
Live state does not confirm this attempt

entries.title: A replacement Executor without the ledger row reported CONFLICT for a write that was applied
entries.impact: Fixed in code; live verification is left to P3.01 and P4.01. An Executor that finds the resourceVersion moved now looks for this action's evidence annotation on the Deployment and reports APPLIED for a peer's write without writing again. A host given a reconcile command with no ledger row journals the action as in doubt and reconciles from the proposal and live state, so it never starts that write. An execute command on a fresh host can still write, and the resourceVersion test in the patch lets at most one write for the action commit. Decision-table and integration tests cover both. One gap stays: if the peer's write was later overwritten, execute() reports CONFLICT where reconcile() reports SUPERSEDED; the Coordinator records both as FAILED. No run has used more than one Executor host; the 2026-11-11 live runs each used one.
entries.workaround: Run one Executor with one ledger directory, as every documented run does, until a multi-host run verifies this.

cites.text: # Another host may already have committed this same action.
# Journal the action as in doubt here, so this host can never start it.
Every worker must use the same ledger and lock directory

entries.title: Lifecycle ordering compares wall-clock timestamps written by different components
entries.impact: The Coordinator refuses a result whose timestamp is not later than the evidence it follows. If the Executor's clock is behind the Guard's, an applied execution result is refused with HTTP 400, and the remote worker retries it forever because it gives up only on 404 or 409. Lease renewal also mixes the Coordinator's and the worker's clocks.
entries.workaround: Run every component on one host, so they share one clock. All committed runs did.

entries.title: Agent mode bypasses the durable Planner journal
entries.impact: Agent planning calls the RCA engine directly instead of the PlannerStore journal. A failed agent run saves no ESCALATE, nothing retries it, and the incident stays OPEN.
entries.workaround: Read the run's summary.json and dashboard event, then handle the incident by hand. The harness removes the fault as an administrator restore, which is not Sentinel recovery.

entries.title: No live run yet shows a person approving through the authenticated API
entries.impact: Fixed in code: every live harness path (Executor experiment, Boutique walkthrough, provider mode and agent mode) now creates approvals through the authenticated approval API, served per run by a child process with generated tokens, and the Executor's final pre-write lookup reads them through ApprovalClient. Revocation, expiry or a stopped authority therefore fails closed with zero writes, and agent mode no longer records a pre-authorised approval. An interactive run needs a person to type the exact action ID; an unattended run must opt in to auto-lab approval, recorded under the automated-lab identity and never as a person. This is proven offline with the real child process and a fake Kubernetes API. Live verification pending: no live run has used this path, so no evidence yet shows a person approving, and every committed live bundle used pre-authorised lab approval. The file-backed negative cases still give the Executor a fixed approval record that never reaches the Coordinator; they prove refusals only. Identities are bearer tokens over loopback HTTP, not a per-person login.
entries.workaround: Treat committed live results as lab approval. For new evidence of a person deciding, run with -Approval interactive (the default) and check operator_approval in summary.json.

cites.text: record if approval and not coordinator else None

entries.title: Raw container log text reaches the model
entries.impact: Container log lines are exported and quoted into model context. A crafted log line could steer the model towards a rollback to the measured baseline. Guard and the Executor still enforce the target, baseline and resourceVersion checks.
entries.workaround: None in code. The prompt tells the model that telemetry is untrusted, which is not a control.

entries.title: Structured logs cover only the networked entrypoints, and no live run has collected them
entries.impact: Fixed in code for the networked processes: shared/log.py writes allowlisted JSON lines; the Coordinator server, worker HTTP, approval HTTP and worker service entrypoints configure it; every POST request gets one http.access line, or an auth.denied line for a 401 or 403, while GET /healthz, GET /readyz and GET requests for unknown paths (404) get none; lifecycle transitions are journalled; and every broad except handler re-raises or logs the error class, which CI enforces. Not covered: the live harnesses (the Executor wedge harness included), agent mode and the in-process pipelines that every recorded run used never configure logging, so their log events are dropped. Exception messages are never logged, only class names, by design. There is no cross-process tracing. No live run has collected logs yet.
entries.workaround: For recorded runs, read the per-run JSON evidence files and the dashboard event journal. For networked runs, collect each process's stderr with SENTINEL_LOG_FORMAT=json.

cites.text: any read failure leaves the outcome unknown
only when their entrypoint configures logging

entries.title: A Deployment scaled to zero replicas is treated as healthy
entries.impact: With no other failure signal, desired replicas of 0 produce no incident, so an accidental scale-down is not detected.
entries.workaround: None. Only the invalid-PORT fault is in scope today.

entries.title: The Coordinator is one process with one SQLite file
entries.impact: No replica takes over if the Coordinator host or its volume is lost; work waits until it returns. Workers back off for up to 60 s, which lengthens recovery after a restart.
entries.workaround: Restart the Coordinator on the same volume; saved requests replay from SQLite.

entries.title: The Executor ledger and target locks are host-local
entries.impact: Two Executors on different hosts would not exclude each other. Safety would then rest on the resourceVersion-conditional patch alone.
entries.workaround: Run every Executor on one host with one ledger and lock directory.

cites.text: These locks do not implement distributed leases or fencing across hosts.

entries.title: No fencing of abandoned or revoked writes across hosts
entries.impact: Revocation is check-then-act: a kubectl patch can land up to 15 s after the last authority check, and the resourceVersion test does not stop a stale write if nobody else wrote in between. RBAC limits verbs and resources, not Deployment fields.
entries.workaround: Single-host runs only; the restricted adapter supplies the exact conditional JSON Patch.

cites.text: Kubernetes RBAC limits resources/verbs, not individual Deployment fields

entries.title: The networked worker layer has only run on one host
entries.impact: The HTTPS delivery layer is tested in-process over 127.0.0.1. It has never run as separate processes, containers or nodes under network faults. Containers or kind nodes on one Docker host would still not be separate machines.
entries.workaround: None; read the distributed design as untested beyond one host.

entries.title: One fault type and one repair action
entries.impact: Every live recovery is an invalid shipping PORT where ROLLBACK is always right, so no result shows a choice between actions. RESTART and SCALE are in the contract, but Guard and the Executor refuse them.
entries.workaround: Quote results only for this fault and action.

cites.text: Only explicit baseline ROLLBACK is implemented.

entries.title: No diagnosis-accuracy evaluation
entries.impact: There is no committed RCAEval result and no comparison of retrieval alone, retrieval with validation, and full Sentinel. Agent results show recovery on one fault, not diagnosis accuracy.
entries.workaround: None; do not quote agent recovery counts as accuracy.

entries.title: Only one fault at a time has been verified
entries.impact: Concurrent incidents queue per workload in code, but two simultaneous faults and dependency-safe recovery have never been run live.
entries.workaround: Inject one fault per run.

entries.title: Model cold loads make agent planning slow and variable
entries.impact: Incident-to-repair time in agent mode had a long tail (docs/results.md). The two measured cold calls took up to 41 s with model loads up to 26 s, and one 356 s decision stage holds only 53 s of recorded model calls, so its cause is not established. The bounded transport is in code: each model call has an overall deadline, a response size cap, no redirects or proxies and a schema check; agent mode runs a preflight and a warm-up call before any fault is injected and records model-runtime.json; keep_alive is configurable. Measured live on 4afc879 (C-AGENT-RECORDED: three runs on one Windows host, 2026-11-11): with qwen3:14b Q4_K_M fully on the GPU and keep_alive 30m, all nine model calls were warm (load under 1 s), model time per run was 21.9 to 24.0 s and incident to Guard ALLOW took 23.3 to 25.6 s; the first run's warm-up loaded the model in 18.6 s before the fault was injected. The preflight stopped a missing model before fault injection (C-AGENT-PREFLIGHT-RECORDED). Not measured: a cold load during a run with the bounded transport, so the tail after an evicted or cold model is unknown. The per-call timeout still defaults to 300 s; P2.01 puts agent planning under a planning budget.
entries.workaround: Keep the model warm with keep_alive and check the warm-up load time in model-runtime.json after each run.

entries.title: The security lab protects only the shipping path
entries.impact: The other Boutique services accept plaintext from any Pod and have no NetworkPolicy. The protected lab has never been combined with guarded recovery.
entries.workaround: Quote security results for the shipping path only.

cites.text: Only the shipping path is protected

entries.title: Workload image CVEs raise alerts but gate nothing
entries.impact: The 11 November evaluation found High or Critical findings in 11 of 13 images. The scan monitor raises dashboard alerts; nothing in Guard, admission or CI blocks a vulnerable image. CI now fails on known vulnerabilities in the locked Python packages (pip-audit) and the dashboard's npm packages, but it scans no image.
entries.workaround: Review scan alerts by hand before a demo.

entries.title: Sentinel component images used unpinned base image tags
entries.impact: Fixed in code: every FROM line, the frontend stage included, is pinned by digest, a test fails on an unpinned base, and Dependabot proposes digest updates. It is recorded as mitigated, not fixed, until the pull request that merges it is known. Images built for earlier evidence used unpinned bases.
entries.workaround: Not needed for new builds. Record the built image id with each run.

entries.title: Chaos Mesh faults are injection only, and HTTP and DNS faults do not run on this host
entries.impact: Sentinel takes no recovery action on Chaos Mesh faults. The HTTP fault needs a kernel module the Docker Desktop WSL2 kernel lacks, and the DNS fault needs a shell the hardened Boutique pods do not have.
entries.workaround: Use the CPU, memory, Pod and network faults as injection demonstrations only.

cites.text: DNSChaos needs a shell and a writable /etc

entries.title: Most committed evidence has inferred provenance
entries.impact: Bundles collected before provenance stamping carry a best-guess revision: every chaos, security-lab, observer, packaged, shipping-lab, provider-recovery and ui-session bundle, the four earlier connected-harness runs, the two earlier Guard rejections and 20 agent runs. Recorded bundles now exist for the cited live classes: one connected-harness run, one Guard rejection with zero Executor patch attempts and four agent runs from 4afc879 on 2026-11-11 (C-CONNECTED-HARNESS-RECORDED, C-GUARD-REJECTION-RECORDED, C-AGENT-RECORDED, C-AGENT-PREFLIGHT-RECORDED), plus the offline Guard evaluation. The three Executor wedge bundles are inferred: the harness summary has no provenance block, so each revision is the operator's statement in the MANIFEST basis. Every live run is on one Windows host, and no release tag ties the evidence to a frozen artefact.
entries.workaround: Quote each claim with its scope caveat, which names its provenance, and prefer the claims whose bundles are recorded.

entries.title: No tagged, scanned release image
entries.impact: The packaged runner is built locally from the checkout. It was rebuilt and scanned for PR #98, but no image is tagged or published, and that scan is not a committed evidence bundle.
entries.workaround: Build the runner from the revision you are testing.

entries.title: Security lab certificates are two-day fixtures with no rotation
entries.impact: Certificates expire after two days and are not rotated, revoked or bound to a workload identity.
entries.workaround: Recreate the lab for each session.

entries.title: The Verifier judged NOT_RECOVERED on its first reading after a patch
entries.impact: A repair that worked was recorded as failed while gRPC clients were still reconnecting, so agent runs ended NOT_RECOVERED.
entries.workaround: Not needed; an opt-in convergence grace sets aside only a leading run of unhealthy readings.

entries.title: An executor.reconcile command was processed as a new execution
entries.impact: A reconcile command could start a write instead of only inspecting a journaled one.
entries.workaround: Not needed.

cites.text: A reconcile command may only inspect a write, never start one.

entries.title: The Guard held a SQLite write lock across kubectl and passed target names unchecked
entries.impact: A slow cluster read blocked other workers for up to 30 s, and a target name could be parsed by kubectl as an option.
entries.workaround: Not needed.

entries.title: Agent planning failures were not shown on the dashboard or in summary.json
entries.impact: A failed agent run looked like a stalled one, and Ollama's own error text was discarded. The incident still stays OPEN; see L-AGENT-JOURNAL.
entries.workaround: Not needed.

cites.text: Agent planning stopped; no repair proposed

entries.title: The documented Chaos Mesh network, Pod and DNS scenarios could not run as written
entries.impact: Chaos Mesh rejected the network scenario, the Pod fault run was always marked failed, and the DNS fault could not work on the hardened pods.
entries.workaround: Not needed; DNS is now refused before any cluster work.

entries.title: One failed kubectl read during Verifier sampling aborted the pass
entries.impact: A single transient read error ended verification with no outcome.
entries.workaround: Not needed.

entries.title: The packaged runner failed on a UTF-8 console
entries.impact: A byte-order mark before the image stream made the image import fail on code page 65001.
entries.workaround: Not needed.

entries.title: Lab scripts left the user's kubectl context changed or unset
entries.impact: Creating and deleting lab clusters in the default kubeconfig left the user's context pointing elsewhere or unset. Follow-up fixes for the other launchers are PRs #95 and #96.
entries.workaround: Not needed.
